question.text: An electric bulb rated as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is used in a circuit having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> supply. The resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> that must be put in series with the bulb so that the bulb delivers the same power is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Power, P=V2RB

RB=V2P=100×100200

RB=50 Ω

To produce same power, same voltage (i.e., 100 V) should be across the bulb. 

Hence, R=RB

R=50 Ω
